summary.text: Lew Wasserman is the Democratic candidate for Florida State Senate District 22 in the November 3, 2026 general election, in a race with Republican James Buchanan and Martin Hyde, who has no party affiliation.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as an attorney, educator and public servant.

paragraphs.text: Lew Wasserman said in a Ballotpedia survey that he earned a Ph.D. in psychology from Hofstra University and a J.D. from St. John's University, which he attended at night.
He said that, as an attorney, he worked on class-action and constitutional cases, including cases on the rights of children with disabilities and of people facing workplace discrimination.
Before practicing law, he said, he was an assistant superintendent of schools in a district serving more than 10,000 students, and he later taught graduate courses at the University of Texas.
Wasserman advanced from the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot because the primary was canceled.

In the survey, he named housing and insurance affordability, local control of local decisions, and protection of water, wetlands and natural lands in Sarasota and Manatee counties as key campaign messages.
He also said he supports expanding Medicaid and using the state's purchasing and regulatory power to address health care costs, including prescription drug prices.
